extracted.intended_audience: academics, researchers, and authors (humanities, social sciences, business) considering publishing a book with Palgrave Macmillan
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on publishing academic books and chapters (monographs, reference works, handbooks, textbooks, and shorter formats) with Palgrave Macmillan, including format selection, open access options, peer review, and submission routes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose the right book format
rubrics_metrics.description: Palgrave Macmillan publishes books and contributed volumes in different formats across the humanities, social sciences, and business; the various publication formats vary in length, range, and depth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the format and scope that best align with your research objectives and desired impact. The site points authors to a step-by-step guide and resources to explore format options before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial support and rigorous peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: All Palgrave Macmillan books benefit from expert editorial support and are subject to rigorous peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can expect an in-house editorial team to support the publication journey; editorial standards apply equally to open access and non-open access books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access option and its benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: You can choose to publish your academic book or chapter open access, making it freely available to anyone with internet access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open access allows unrestricted online access, authors retain copyright and can comply with funders' mandates. Palgrave reports average performance metrics for open access books: ~10× more downloads, ~2.4× more citations, ~10× more online mentions, and ~61% more country reach compared to non-open access titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monograph suitability and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer-reviewed monographs explore evolving and cutting-edge research areas (examples given: cybersecurity, mathematical finance, agricultural economics, environmental humanities, sustainability, artificial intelligence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monographs can be published independently or as part of established book series; authors across humanities, social sciences, and business publish monographs with Palgrave. Monographs are discoverable via Springer Nature Link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major Reference Works: living reference model
rubrics_metrics.description: Major Reference Works are authoritative, comprehensive overviews of substantial breadth and depth on a central topic; Palgrave publishes these using an online-first Living Reference Model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Living Reference Model means entries are continuously updated through a dynamic, peer-reviewed publishing process; individual entries are available online once ready, are citable by DOI (including updated material), and the in-house editorial team collaborates with the editor-in-chief. Manuscript processing is handled via the Meteor submission platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Palgrave Handbooks: commissioned, agenda-setting collections
rubrics_metrics.description: Palgrave Handbooks bring together specially-commissioned chapters, cutting-edge research, and the latest review articles to provide an unparalleled overview of a specific field and to set the agenda for future directions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handbooks are original reference works designed to be comprehensive and to define research trajectories in their disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional business and professional finance books: audience and style
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional business and professional finance books feature authoritative and accessible texts for business and finance professionals, from graduate employees to chief executives and managing directors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These titles should be practitioner-relevant and written accessibly while maintaining authority; target readership ranges across career stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Palgrave Pivot: concise, timely research format
rubrics_metrics.description: Palgrave Pivot combines speed with quality, offering authors a concise format of 25,000–50,000 words; longer than an article but shorter than a monograph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pivot reduces time to publication without compromising editorial standards, making it suitable for emerging areas and timely issues (examples: global financial crisis, Brexit, COVID-19) and for work that wishes to reach beyond academia to practitioners and policy audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Palgrave Textbooks: scope and audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Palgrave publishes textbooks for students at all levels, from first-year undergraduate to postgraduate and beyond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Textbooks are accessibly written and rigorously reviewed, aimed at students across social sciences, humanities, business, economics, finance, politics, and international studies; they should provide up-to-date content to enhance understanding and encourage thoughtful learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing in a Palgrave book series
rubrics_metrics.description: Palgrave Macmillan book series foster in-depth and impactful scholarly dialogue and connect publications with related research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing in an established series lends credibility and recognition; series titles receive expert input and dedicated promotion to maximise visibility and reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits of publishing with Palgrave
rubrics_metrics.description: When you publish with Palgrave Macmillan, you'll benefit from a supportive editorial experience and global marketing and distribution, to enable your work to achieve its full potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should weigh publisher-provided services (editorial support, marketing, distribution) as part of choosing where and how to publish their work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit your book idea: early-stage engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: If you already have an idea for a book, even in the early stages, you can fill out this form, with no obligation, to get personal support in growing it into a book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting an idea initiates personal support from the publisher; the page frames the submission form as a low-commitment first step in the publication process.
